items_missed: No agenda statement — opened with 'did you have any questions for me' instead of framing what the call would cover and how long it would take; no 'sound good?'

Probing was thin: never asked about stairs or floors at either location, elevator, parking, loading access, long walks or narrow hallways, packing needs, box count, storage stops, or additional stops — and this is an office building
Never asked about moving stressors or what she was worried about
Never read the origin/destination addresses back to confirm them, despite noting the profile was missing all the scope notes
What's-included was a vague 'everything's included, if you can think of it, it's included' — never itemized truck, gas, taxes, insurance, blankets, wrap, bands, tools
No Meet Your Mover email description
No On-Time Guarantee — explained the 2-hour arrival window in detail but never said Einstein starts discounting if it's missed, which was the natural moment for it

Clock section almost entirely skipped: never said the clock starts on site when the contract opens, never explained 15-minute prorated billing after the minimum, no 'does that make sense?' sense-check
Save Your Ass prep speech not given at all — zero prep, consolidation, or carload tips
Did not mention the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or ask her to reply with corrections
Never gave business hours or how to reach the branch
Used her name once ('Hey, Amy') — needs 3+
top_strength: He caught that the inherited 3.5-hour estimate was a software default with no notes behind it, rebuilt the scope himself (12 pieces of furniture, nothing over 250 lbs, no antiques), corrected it down to 2.5 hours or less, and that correction unlocked the Saturday afternoon slot the customer actually wanted but had been told was unavailable. He also proactively offered to put her on a cancellation list for an earlier arrival.
coaching_note: Khevan rescued a badly documented handoff and won the booking, but he skipped the clock explanation and every differentiator — she agreed to $545 without ever hearing how billing works past the minimum, which is exactly how day-of surprises start. Run the full clock and differentiator block even on warm callbacks that feel like a formality.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and natural — owned the handoff gap without excuses, used easy affirmations ('Beautiful', 'Easy enough'), and volunteered the cancellation list unprompted; the customer stayed relaxed and positive throughout.
